newsitem.title: USA: U.S. retailers carrying leaner inventories.
newsitem.headline: U.S. retailers carrying leaner inventories.

text.p: U.S. retailers, many reporting strong November sales on Thursday, carried relatively lean inventories during the month that enabled them to put off some profit-cutting promotions, industry analysts said.
"Inventories are in good shape...we're looking for reduced clearance markdown activity in January, so that bodes well for profits," Saul Yaari, an analyst with Piper Jaffrey, said.
Yaari, however, noted that December would see more discounts than November.
Analysts agreed that the store chains were not panicking, as some did in last season's dismal holiday shopping season.

"Inventory seems to be under control so you shouldn't see a lot of margin pressure," said Dain Bosworth analyst Dean Ramos. The Dain Bosworth November same-store sales index registerd a 3.7 percent rise, compared with 3.1 percent last year.
"It looks as though there is not much panic liquidation," Ramos said.
The exception, however, is seen in the consumer electronics industry, where the lack of a hot product like last year's Windows 95 has curtailed sales.

"Promotions in consumer electronics were atrocious, I mean really terrible (for retailers' profits)," Yaari said, citing computer monitor and television giveaways with other purchases. He said he plans to cut earnings estimates for some consumer electronics retailers.
